steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have things been since you finished the body contouring program with us? I usually hear one of three things. Still holding your results, a little starting to creep back, or pretty much back to how it was. Which one is closest for you?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Doing Great
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's exactly what we hope for when someone finishes treatment with us. {{provider_name}} will be glad to know you're still happy with the results.

(Let them respond, then continue.)

steps.title: Starting to Creep Back
steps.content:
That happens, {{contact_first_name}}. Without the sessions and the plan, things tend to come back over time. It's not anything you did wrong. Your notes say you were really happy with how it turned out. What kept you from coming back in?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Pretty Much Back to Before
steps.content:
I'm sorry to hear that, {{contact_first_name}}. Without the sessions and the plan, things tend to come back over time. It's not anything you did wrong. Your notes say you were really happy with the results. Was it cost, timing, or something else that kept you from coming back?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
While I have you, {{contact_first_name}}, can I ask you a few quick questions about anything else you've noticed?

(Wait for the yes. It's their file, so almost everyone says yes.)

steps.title: The Transition: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you said the area we treated is starting to creep back. We'll come back to that. First, can I ask you a few quick questions so your file is up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down every area they name. You'll recap them in a moment.)

First, the lower belly. Anything there that stays the same no matter what the scale says?

How about the sides, the love handle area?

And your upper arms?

What about under the chin?

How are your clothes fitting, anything gotten snug in one spot?

And how's your energy and recovery, by the end of the day or after a workout?

(Recap what you wrote down, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, of those, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask a few quick questions about {{main_concern}} so your file is up to date. It'll only take a minute.

(Ask these three questions in order. Pause after each and let them answer.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a few weeks, or more like months?

(Let them answer.)

Is it something you notice now and then, or every time you look in the mirror?

(Let them answer.)

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with photos, going out, or feeling put together?

(Let them answer. Repeat back whatever they name.)

Thank you for sharing that. It makes sense, and it's something we help people with all the time.

steps.title: The Review
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I have this right.

(Read back their three answers: how long, how often, what it gets in the way of.)

So it's been on your mind a while, and you notice it most times you look in the mirror. At its worst it gets in the way of what you mentioned. Did I get that right?

(Say what they named: photos, going out, or feeling put together. Let them answer. If they correct you, take the correction and move on.)

And it sounds like you'd really like to look in the mirror and feel good about it again. Is that fair to say?

(Most people say yes. Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's worth getting looked at instead of just dealing with it. Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so {{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}}. If we can help, we'll walk you through the options. If it's not the right fit, we'll say so. Either way you'll know where you stand. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you said {{main_concern}} is something you'd like to feel better about. I don't want to assume anything. Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy about it. No pressure. Do not repeat the concern back at them. Let them answer.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: Why Did They Stop?
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad everything is still holding up so well.

Can I ask what changed that led you to stop coming in?

(Let them answer. Listen all the way through. Do not argue with it.)

Keeping your results takes a lot less than it took to build them. A check-in now and then keeps them working for you. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in for a check-in so you keep what you've got. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Objection: “It came back after I stopped”
steps.content:
That happens. It's hard to hold everything on your own once the sessions stop. That's why coming in makes sense, so we can look at the whole picture and make a plan.

Can we get you in so we can take a look?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m embarrassed it came back”
steps.content:
Please don't be. This happens to almost everyone once treatments stop. That's the reason we call. We'd just like to help you get back to where you were.

Would you be open to that?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Objection: “Did it even work last time?”
steps.content:
That's a fair question, and it's the kind of thing we'd want to talk through in person. That way we can look at the whole picture and see what would help it hold.

(Do not promise results on the call.)

Is there anything else on your mind?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think about it”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask what part you'd want to think over? Sometimes it's the cost, sometimes the timing, and sometimes people just want to be sure it's right for them.

(Listen. Their answer usually points to one of the buttons below. If it stays general, keep going.)

Coming in is really just information. You'd see what's possible and what it would involve, and then you decide with real answers. No pressure either way.

Does that help?

steps.title: Objection: “Just send me some info”
steps.content:
I'd be glad to send you some information, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd say is that a flyer can only tell you so much. It can't show you what's possible for you specifically. That's what a quick visit is for. So let me get you on the schedule first, and then I'll send the information along.

Does that work for you?
